# 1 Clement Chapter 35 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 35 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_035_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 35

**35:1** How blessed and marvelous are the gifts of God, beloved! Life in immortality, splendor in righteousness, truth in boldness, faith in confidence, self-control in holiness; and all these fall under our understanding.

**35:2** What then are the things being prepared for those who wait for him? The Creator and Father of the ages, the All-holy, himself knows their greatness and beauty.

**35:3** Let us therefore make every effort to be found in the number of those who wait, that we may receive a share of the promised gifts.

**35:4** But how shall this be, beloved? If our mind is set upon God through faith; if we seek out the things that are well-pleasing and acceptable to him; if we accomplish the things that accord with his blameless will, and if we follow the way of truth, throwing far from us all unrighteousness and iniquity, greed, strife, malice and deceit, whispering and slander, hatred of God, pride and boastfulness, vainglory and inhospitality.

**35:5** For those who do these things are hateful to God; and not only those who do them, but also those who approve them.

**35:6** For the scripture says: "But to the sinner God said: Why do you declare my statutes and take up my covenant in your mouth?

**35:7** But you hated instruction and cast my words behind you. If you saw a thief, you ran along with him, and with adulterers you shared your lot. Your mouth has multiplied wickedness, and your tongue has woven deceit. Sitting down you spoke against your brother, and you placed a stumbling block against your mother's son.

**35:8** These things you did and I was silent; you thought, wicked man, that I would be like you. I will reprove you and set your case before your face.

**35:9** Understand these things, you who forget God, lest he seize you like a lion and there be none to deliver you.

**35:10** The sacrifice of praise will glorify me, and that is the way by which I will show him God's salvation."

---

*EMET renders with maximal literalness. The extended Psalm 50 LXX (Psalm 49 LXX) citation in vv. 6-10 is the longest scripture quotation in chapters 23-44. It reinforces Clement's warning against hypocrisy and covenant-breaking.*
